correspondance-famille-lot-10-cartes-pos.subtitle: From 1916 to the 1950s · 10 handwritten cards
correspondance-famille-lot-10-cartes-pos.description:
Ten written postcards, kept together for nearly a century. From one card to the next you find the same first names (Agnès, Germaine, Constant, Ginette, Solange…) and the same places, like the Bois-Hamon, from where letters were written to the family. It is a real thread of life, which is why they are sold together.

Some cards also carry small pieces of history. On 4 March 1925, a young telephone operator of the 8th regiment writes to his brother and sister from the camp at Griesheim, in occupied Germany. In June 1941, a card sent from Savenay tells of the black market: “you can’t find anything any more, it’s the hunger diet, just like where you are”.

In the lot:
· Griesheim, the telephone exchange: blue card written in 1925
· San José Mission, San Antonio (Texas): American “Post Card”, written in Savenay on 29 June 1941
· “L’Amour dans le cœur”: REX 1334 fancy card, medallions and garland of roses
· Girl with a bouquet: S.L. Paris 3040 photo card
· “Je meurs où je m’attache”: ivy and medallion of children
· Le Langage des fleurs (mistletoe, rose, holly, ivy, honeysuckle): publisher G. Harel, Paris
· Bonne Année with roses: publisher SAP 1456
· Bonne Année with a baby among roses
· Saint-Céré (Lot), the quays and the schools: hand-coloured card, a letter from Solange to Agnès
· Nemours, the Beauregard viewpoint indicator: card with deckled edges

On the backs you can also read letters dated Paris, 20 May 1916, Bois-Hamon, 2 August and 31 December 1925, and Christmas 1924.

Condition: these are period cards, with rubbed corners, foxing, small stains and a water mark at the top of one card. The photos show everything. In the photos on the site the addresses are blurred; the cards themselves are sent intact.

Sent by letter post, in a stiffened envelope.

pichet-verre-murano-scavo-blanc-mures-ap.description:
A jug blown in the “scavo” technique, the Murano speciality that imitates Roman glass fresh from an excavation: a matt, satiny surface, a milky white veil, tiny bubbles trapped in the glass and earth-coloured sandy deposits deliberately left during firing.

The shape echoes antique pitchers: a round belly, a tall flared neck circled by two trails of spun glass, an applied handle. The decoration is entirely hot-applied: clustered fruit like raised mulberries, a stylised lion’s head and a round medallion on the belly. The iridescent sheen on the neck and handle is typical of this glass.

Under the base, the pontil mark confirms it was blown by hand.

Scavo glass was developed in Murano from the 1950s, notably by Gino Cenedese and Antonio Da Ros, then taken up by several of the island’s glassworks. This piece is not signed: it is sold as Murano scavo glass, with no attribution to a specific workshop.

Dimensions: height 18 cm, width 10 cm.

Condition: lovely, with signs of use. The beige deposits and the veil are part of the technique, not dirt. A fine horizontal line is visible at the top of the neck in one photo: check it closely in the real photos before buying.

A striking decorative piece, superb on its own on a shelf or with a few dried branches. A one-of-a-kind object, sent very well protected or handed over in person in Rennes.
